```{python}
#| label: fig-fabric-shape
#| fig-cap: "Where a failure lands, counted in records. In a tree (a) the interior node holds the index over its subtree, so losing it leaves every record beneath intact on its own medium and unreadable through the fabric: nothing is damaged, and nothing in that subtree can be found. In the fabric each peer indexes only the coordinates it answers for, so a lost peer costs its own records (b); a peer that builds no index loses the same records and answers more slowly (c). Loss tracks who is authoritative for a coordinate, while the index moves read cost and reachability. Replicating the interior node in (a) buys the same reachability by keeping a second copy of the index in step; the fabric removes the shared state rather than duplicating it."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "font.serif": ["STIXGeneral", "Times New Roman", "DejaVu Serif"],
    "font.size": 7,
})

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(7.4, 2.6))


def peer(ax, x, y, lines, failed=False, w=0.30, h=0.145):
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch(
        (x - w / 2, y - h / 2), w, h,
        boxstyle="round,pad=0.006,rounding_size=0.018",
        facecolor="0.90" if failed else "white",
        edgecolor="black",
        linewidth=1.4 if failed else 0.7,
        linestyle=(0, (2.5, 1.6)) if failed else "solid",
        zorder=3))
    ax.text(x, y + 0.021, lines[0], ha="center", va="center",
            fontsize=6.4, zorder=4)
    ax.text(x, y - 0.023, lines[1], ha="center", va="center",
            fontsize=6.4, color="0.30", zorder=4)


def link(ax, a, b):
    ax.plot([a[0], b[0]], [a[1], b[1]], color="black", lw=0.6, zorder=1)


# (a) a tree: one interior node holds the index over its subtree
a = axes[0]
root = (0.50, 0.80)
leaves = [(0.17, 0.40), (0.50, 0.40), (0.83, 0.40)]
for leaf in leaves:
    link(a, root, leaf)
peer(a, *root, ["0 records", "index 18"], failed=True)
for leaf in leaves:
    peer(a, *leaf, ["6 records", "no index"], w=0.27, h=0.135)
a.text(0.02, 0.99, "(a) a tree, index at the interior node",
       transform=a.transAxes, ha="left", va="top", fontsize=7.4,
       fontweight="bold")
a.text(0.5, 0.06, "readable after the failure\n0 of 18, all intact and unreadable",
       ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=6.8)

# (b) the fabric: each peer indexes its own coordinates
b = axes[1]
peers_b = [(0.20, 0.74), (0.80, 0.74), (0.50, 0.36)]
for i in range(3):
    for j in range(i + 1, 3):
        link(b, peers_b[i], peers_b[j])
peer(b, *peers_b[0], ["6 records", "index 6"], w=0.27, h=0.135)
peer(b, *peers_b[1], ["6 records", "index 6"], failed=True, w=0.27, h=0.135)
peer(b, *peers_b[2], ["6 records", "index 6"], w=0.27, h=0.135)
b.text(0.02, 0.99, "(b) the fabric, each peer indexed",
       transform=b.transAxes, ha="left", va="top", fontsize=7.4,
       fontweight="bold")
b.text(0.5, 0.06, "readable after the failure\n12 of 18, 6 lost with the peer",
       ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=6.8)

# (c) the fabric without an index: the same loss, a slower answer
c = axes[2]
peers_c = [(0.20, 0.74), (0.80, 0.74), (0.50, 0.36)]
for i in range(3):
    for j in range(i + 1, 3):
        link(c, peers_c[i], peers_c[j])
peer(c, *peers_c[0], ["6 records", "no index"], w=0.27, h=0.135)
peer(c, *peers_c[1], ["6 records", "no index"], failed=True, w=0.27, h=0.135)
peer(c, *peers_c[2], ["6 records", "no index"], w=0.27, h=0.135)
c.text(0.02, 0.99, "(c) the fabric, no index built",
       transform=c.transAxes, ha="left", va="top", fontsize=7.4,
       fontweight="bold")
c.text(0.5, 0.06, "readable after the failure\n12 of 18, 6 lost, reads slower",
       ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=6.8)

for ax in axes:
    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.axis("off")

fig.tight_layout(pad=0.2)
plt.show()
```
